# sitegen

Static site generator for a small blog. Builds `content/` Markdown into `out/` HTML.

## Layout

- `content/posts/*.md` -- blog posts (front-matter: title, date)
- `content/index.md`, `content/about.md` -- top-level pages
- `templates/page.html` -- shared template with `{{title}}`, `{{nav}}`, `{{stylesheet}}`, `{{content}}` placeholders
- `static/style.css` -- shared stylesheet
- `build.py` -- build script (stdlib only)
- `tests/test_build.py` -- unit tests

## Build & test

    python3 build.py
    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v

## Key behavior

- Posts go to `out/posts/<slug>.html`; top-level pages to `out/<slug>.html`
- Nav and stylesheet links use relative prefixes (posts use `../`)
- Index lists all posts sorted by date (newest first)
- Markdown subset: headings (#, ##, ###), paragraphs, links, **bold**

## Known pitfall & fix

Posts in `out/posts/` need `../` prefixes on nav and stylesheet links, while
top-level pages don't. `render_page` takes a `prefix` parameter — pass `"../"`
for posts, `""` for top-level pages. The template uses `{{stylesheet}}` and
`{{nav}}` placeholders so the prefix is applied consistently.

**Fix is applied and verified (2026-09-18):** `render_page(title, body, prefix)` in `build.py`
replaces the hardcoded `href="style.css"` in the template with `href="{{stylesheet}}"` and
passes `prefix` to `nav_html()`. Posts call it with `prefix="../"`, top-level pages with
`prefix=""`. Verified: build + 5/5 unit tests pass; all pages and the stylesheet return
200 over HTTP; post pages use `../style.css` and `../index.html`.

**Symptom if it breaks again:** post pages (`out/posts/*.html`) lose their CSS
and nav links 404 — `href="style.css"` resolves to `out/posts/style.css` which
doesn't exist. Build succeeds but the site looks broken in a browser.

## Adding a post

input.content:
# sitegen

A small static site generator for a blog. Turns `content/` Markdown into a browsable site under `out/`.

## Quick start

```bash
# Build the site
python3 build.py

# Preview it (serves out/ on http://localhost:8000)
cd out && python3 -m http.server

# Run the test suite
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

## Adding a post

1. Create `content/posts/my-post.md`:

```markdown
---
title: My post title
date: 2026-09-18
---

# My post title

A paragraph of text. **Bold** works. [Links](https://example.com) too.

## A subheading

Another paragraph.
```

2. Run `python3 build.py`
3. The post automatically appears on the index, listed by date (newest first).
4. The post's URL is `out/posts/my-post.html`.

## Project layout

```
content/
  index.md            # Homepage (lists all posts)
  about.md            # Static about page
  posts/              # One .md file per post
templates/
  page.html           # Shared HTML template
static/
  style.css           # Single stylesheet
build.py              # The build script (stdlib only)
out/                  # Generated output — do not edit by hand
```

## Front-matter

Every file can have a `---` delimited header:

```markdown
---
title: Required — becomes the <title> tag and the heading
date: Used for sorting posts on the index
---
```

If `title` is missing, the filename is used.

## Markdown subset

The renderer supports only:

- `#`, `##`, `###` headings
- Paragraphs (blank-line separated)
- `**bold**`
- `[text](url)` links

That's it. It's deliberate — it keeps the build script under a hundred lines.

## How it works

`build.py` reads `content/posts/*.md`, renders each to HTML using the shared `templates/page.html` template, and writes `out/posts/<slug>.html`. Top-level files (`index.md`, `about.md`) become `out/index.html` and `out/out/about.html`. `style.css` is copied to `out/style.css`. The index page gets an auto-generated list of all posts, sorted by date.

Post pages link to `../style.css` and `../index.html` (they're one directory deep); top-level pages link without the prefix. This is handled by a `prefix` parameter on `render_page`.

## After editing build.py

Run:

```bash
python3 build.py
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Then verify links resolve by serving `out/` and curling the paths — everything should return 200. Watch out for the prefix logic: if post pages lose their CSS or nav links, `../` handling has broken.

Done. Here's what was wrong and what I fixed:

**Bug found:** The skill claimed the `../` prefix fix was applied, but it wasn't. Post pages (`out/posts/*.html`) linked to `style.css` and `index.html` without the `../` prefix — so CSS and nav links 404'd in the browser even though the build succeeded.

**Fix applied to `build.py`:**
- `render_page(title, body, prefix="")` now takes a prefix and passes it to `nav_html()` and to a new `{{stylesheet}}` template placeholder
- Posts call it with `prefix="../"`, top-level pages with `prefix=""`
- Template updated: `href="style.css"` → `href="{{stylesheet}}"`

**Verified:**
- `python3 build.py` — builds clean
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` — 5/5 pass
- All 6 paths (index, about, style.css, 3 posts) return 200 over HTTP
- Post pages now use `../style.css` and `../index.html`

**Handoff prep:**
- Rewrote `README.md` as a proper onboarding doc (quick start, adding posts, project layout, front-matter, Markdown subset, how it works, verification steps)
- Added `.gitignore` (out/, __pycache__/, etc.)
- Updated the skill with a concrete verification command

Your colleague can clone it, read the README, and start writing posts immediately.
